name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Extract an evidence-backed backend dependency PRD from a delivered frontend, then build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify the matching Domainry source-owned application through one project-visible development TODO. The Skill keeps frontend evidence read-only while settling requirements and domain truth, authors declarative backend/model/*.json metadata, and records evidence-located frontend defects as findings for the frontend owner instead of repairing them. Use for frontend-to-Runtime replacement, new backend projects, existing-project increments, metadata-first backend implementation, Runtime integration, full-stack defect routing, and final verification.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Drive every development batch through:

```text
requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done
```

Platform capabilities determine the implementation mapping; they never determine the business facts. Do not start from Dataset, Report, metadata, an Action shape, or another Runtime feature and work backward into a domain model. Settle occurred facts, summaries, simulations, calculation ownership, persistence, and correction before capability discovery. Only two or more unresolved, mutually incompatible choices that change an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow form a product business ambiguity; block only the smallest affected modeling slice. Missing optional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms are not product blockers. Contract discovery and reversible technical defaults are not substitutes for business facts.

The frontend under `frontend/**` is evidence of product demand, not automatically a complete business specification. Inspect routes, screens, typed API contracts, Mock adapters, tests, roles, states, and copy read-only while settling requirements and domain truth; never promote Mock behavior into business truth. This Skill never creates, modifies, or deletes `frontend/**`, frontend component contracts, or Runtime Client SDK assets. Shared Application Delivery still publishes the Runtime Client SDK for an independent frontend Skill; this Builder Skill never fetches, copies, installs, generates, validates, or takes ownership of it. Route each mismatch to the owner proved by the explicit requirement, published Runtime contract, typed frontend API, Mock/tests, and real behavior. A frontend- or Mock-owned mismatch is a finding for owner `frontend`, never a backend workaround or frontend edit.

## Route exactly once

Choose one route before loading supporting resources. Do not combine the routes.

### Whole-project development

For every normal requirements, build, repair, integration, acceptance, or whole-project continuation batch, read [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) **completely before starting** and use it as the only execution workflow. It contains the authoritative TODO/Gate process, full normal-development CLI map, project boundaries, phase rules, required reference routing, Runtime acceptance, and terminal policy. Follow every applicable routed reference it requires. A full batch reads the whole guide; a light batch may omit only TODO sections under the guide's explicit light-batch rules, never guide loading or an applicable authority.

The routing map below is a reachability contract, not permission to read only selected guide sections:

| Moved entrypoint section / contract | Whole-project authority |
| --- | --- |
| workflow, routing, and batch scale | [whole-project workflow](references/development-guide.md#whole-project-workflow) |

### Explicit source-finalization continuation

Use this route only when the caller explicitly requests `source-finalization-continuation`, accepts and freezes upstream requirements/modeling, confirms the current source-finalization checkpoint remains valid, and limits scope exactly to:

```text
valid Actions project check → source finalize → module-focused Go test
```

Run the loaded Skill's resolver once with an explicit project-relative focused package:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --profile source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

Before resolving or resuming this continuation, prove the original Host/Agent turn has actually ended. An outer exec session reporting `Unknown process id`, missing its timing trailer, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence and must never trigger a concurrent Agent against the same session. The returned `continuation` envelope atomically owns this session's three-Gate TODO, synchronized Gate IDs, current checkpoint identity, and exact `run_recipes`. Execute those recipes in order and use no other workflow. Do **not** read `references/development-guide.md`, `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`, or any whole-project reference for this profile.

This route is caller authorization, never inferred from project state. Missing, stale, unsafe, or ambiguous session/checkpoint/CLI identity, a package outside the project, a missing focused package, or a conflicting/partial session TODO fails closed. Do not repair such a conflict by deleting or rewriting managed state. The compact route does not bypass the Host's complete loading of this `SKILL.md` and does not change whole-project behavior.

### Explicit post-apply source-finalization continuation

Use this distinct compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `post-apply-source-finalization-continuation` after a fresh successful `model apply` materialization whose source finalization failed solely on generated project-owned Action placeholders, and the caller has completed those Action sources. It does not accept or alter the already-current `source-finalization-continuation` route.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile post-apply-source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

The resolver validates the current signed backend materialization and its exact machine failure receipt before creating state. That receipt must contain only the structured `project.source_placeholder_remains` diagnostics for Action source in the `backend_technical_contract` check; every independent preflight check must have passed, and only the dependent composition check may be skipped. The current source must be a placeholder-free, finalization-ready evolution of that receipt in which only project-owned `backend/actions/**` paths changed. Runtime Client SDK and frontend materialization receipts are never accepted.

On success the resolver atomically owns one TODO, Gate state, and profile with exactly three ordered one-shot recipes:

```text
project check --scope actions → project source finalize → focused Go test
```

Execute only the returned `run_recipes`. Do not edit, add, reorder, duplicate, reopen, attach evidence to, or invoke the underlying product commands outside the profile runner. Partial state, symlinks, traversal or unbounded package paths, changed materialization/failure/source/CLI identities, a forged receipt, any non-placeholder failure, terminal failure, or a different/extra Gate fails closed with no replacement TODO. A completed terminal profile returns no recipes and never reopens. Do **not** read the whole-project guide, TODO template, or another whole-project reference for this profile.

### Explicit project verification continuation

Use this compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `project-verification-continuation` and thereby accepts and freezes requirements, model, and project source. It is independent from package continuation. Do not load the whole-project guide, TODO template, verification authority, production technical Gates, or Gate runner source.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile project-verification-continuation
```

The Go product checkpoint validates the current backend-only materialization, source finalization and identity, Runtime manifest, and backend Application Delivery binding. Python consumes that checkpoint and atomically owns any required one-Gate TODO/state/profile. If verification is already current, the resolver returns terminal completion with no recipe. Otherwise execute the sole returned machine-owned `project verify --json` recipe exactly once. Never supply a label, kind, Gate ID, argv, or binding. Partial/conflicting/unsafe state, stale profile identity, receipt tampering, an extra or reordered Gate, a repeated terminal command, or a changed pre-execution checkpoint fails closed without replacement.

### Explicit project package continuation

Use this separate compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `project-package-continuation` and thereby accepts and freezes requirements, model, and project source. Do not load the whole-project guide, TODO template, verification authority, production technical Gates, or Gate runner source.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile project-package-continuation
```

The Go product checkpoint requires the current V6 verification plus the same current backend binding/materialization/finalization/source/Runtime identity closure. If the package receipt is current, the resolver returns terminal completion with no recipe. Otherwise it atomically owns one machine Gate and returns only the fixed `project package --json` recipe. Execute it exactly once; never author its label, kind, Gate ID, argv, or bindings. The same partial, conflict, symlink/traversal, stale/tamper, extra/reordered Gate, terminal-repeat, and pre-execution-change cases fail closed without overwriting state or accepting an older receipt.

### Explicit Runtime process continuation

Use this compact route when the caller asks only to recover the already-packaged managed Runtime start/status boundary. Use the current Host session ID for this fresh compact continuation; do not create or reuse a whole-project TODO for that session. It does not require loading the whole-project guide, verification references, TODO template, verification authorities, or Gate runner source. Resolve the machine-owned profile once:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile runtime-process-continuation \
  --runtime-address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>
```

When the session has no TODO, Gate state, or Runtime profile, the resolver atomically creates its canonical two-Gate minimal TODO, synchronized state, and profile. It owns the fixed labels, `runtime_start` → `runtime_status` kinds, Gate IDs, exact argv, source/Runtime/cohort bindings, current packaged bundle, packaged CLI, numeric loopback address, and all pinned identities. The tool guarantees that the actual listener is the requested loopback and records its proof; the Agent adds no bind command or listener check. Stdout is only the compact envelope with the remaining `run_recipes`; execute them in order. Do not supply or author a TODO, label, marker, Gate ID, bundle, command argv, or identity binding yourself. Re-resolve after start to obtain only the status recipe when recovering from compaction. A partial session, non-profile-owned TODO, symlink, extra/reordered/forged Gate, changed address/package/source/CLI identity, stale state, terminal failure, or conflict fails closed without deleting or overwriting caller state; a terminal Gate never reopens.

## Loaded Skill and CLI identity

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact filesystem path of the `SKILL.md` loaded for this task. Every Builder command, resolver, Gate runner, template, and reference must come from that same root. The package has one executable: `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Never discover it through `PATH`, substitute another installed Skill's binary, call Domainry Plane directly, or invent a neighboring command.

For whole-project work, the guide requires the default resolver once at task start and binds `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Host session ID, TODO, compact resume packet, one-time authoring context, and package identity to its result. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. For the explicit continuation, the compact resolver call above supplies and validates the same package CLI identity without loading whole-project context.

## Universal safety and evidence invariants

- Treat Runtime-owned identifiers, hierarchy values, principal claims, cursors, and other canonical representations as opaque. Resolve them through the published typed client, `GET /identity/principal-context`, a formal seed/admin path, or a persisted Runtime result and carry them unchanged. Never construct, trim, pad, normalize, inject, or query Runtime-owned persistence to discover them. A missing formal source blocks the affected journey.
- Keep project-owned authoring in `backend/model/*.json`, referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`, project-owned backend source/tests, and the current session's `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md`. Never hand-edit generated source, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned `.domainry/**` delivery state. Never create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that ignores its generated capabilities.
- `model apply` is the only normal-development release command. Its reviewed `--product-surfaces` value is an integration boundary, never frontend mutation authorization. Repair reported model/input failures and run the same product command through a new round-specific Gate; never reopen a terminal Gate, split publication/materialization, or bypass destructive/evolution review.
- Every check, finalize, and focused-test command must run through its own Gate on its first real execution. The runner serializes each session/Gate across processes from state read through product execution and atomic receipt/state commit, and any passed or failed command receipt makes that Gate terminal. Never run the command directly first, rerun it, search historical receipts, or attach another command's receipt. After repair, add a new round-specific TODO Gate or use a genuinely new Host session. A receipt proves only its original Gate and current bound identities; changed bound content may make its evidence stale but never reopens that Gate.
- Before model authoring, bind every acceptance journey to its requirement, formal actor/session/principal, canonical context and identifiers, isolated setup, command/read surfaces, non-empty positive oracle, exact denied/conflict and unchanged-state oracle, durable effect, and dependencies. Do not create a second plan. Scope-sensitive journeys use same-record contrasts through real Runtime sessions; arbitrary errors, empty results, and residue from another case do not prove success. For unchanged/replay record hashes, use `runtimeRecordDurableSnapshot` (or copied-harness `durable_record_snapshot`), never the whole HTTP response body.
- When a settled requirement explicitly names an initial/default field value, add one TODO checkpoint that records the requirement evidence, exact Object-field JSON Pointer, concrete `default_value`, and its matching option/state entry. Close it only after the pointer exists in the applied model and validation proves membership; never leave the behavior only in acceptance prose or infer a default from silence. The authoritative mapping and applied example are in [CRUD and state machine](references/capabilities/crud-and-state-machine.md).
- After current source finalization and focused tests pass, run one highest-risk semantic canary across formal identity/context resolution → command → persisted effect → actor-visible read-back before broad Runtime integration. A canary failure blocks dependents and is repaired once at its owner; it never shrinks the frozen model or acceptance denominator.
- Never claim above current evidence. Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Completion requires the applicable evidence Gate, an empty finding inventory, the guide's terminal policy, and the TODO consistency check; unresolved product prerequisites are implementation/Foundation defects, not cosmetic limitations.

In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging. The caller-explicit `source-finalization-continuation` and `post-apply-source-finalization-continuation` routes are selected and initialized from the loaded entrypoint before any whole-project resource is read. They never load this guide, the TODO template, or another whole-project reference; each compact Gate-owned envelope is its complete workflow. For every normal whole-project session, use the following initialization unchanged. At the start of an Agent session: 1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once. 2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`. 3. Resolve the session ID from the resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; the temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, borrow, or reuse another session's ID. 4. If `.domainry/development/.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session. 5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`. 6. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan. 8. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; never check later work merely because it happened out of order. Close checkboxes through the evidence Gate's `run`, `attach`, or explicit `mark --status not_applicable` commands, not by writing success prose. Before leaving a stage, require `status --stage --require-complete`. Before any Host resume, first prove the original Agent turn has actually ended; an outer exec wrapper reporting `Unknown process id`, losing its timing output, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence. Never start a second Agent against the same session TODO/Gates while the first may still be alive. 9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes. For `requirements_only`, the formal Gate identity is the deterministic requirements-evidence closure exposed as `requirements`: the mandatory non-empty `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`; root `requirements.md` when it exists; and, when `frontend/src/**` contains a regular source file, the complete regular-file evidence under `frontend/**` after excluding dependency, build, coverage, cache, database, log, backup, and temporary artifacts. Paths and content hashes are sorted and framed, so creation order, timestamps, worktree location, backend files, unrelated root files, and derived frontend files do not affect the identity; symlinks fail closed. A frontend-led or immutable external-reference PRD is valid without root `requirements.md`: the PRD records its authority and immutable frontend snapshot/commit or external citation, and the local frontend closure is bound automatically when present. Do not silently place another mutable local authority elsewhere; make it the canonical root `requirements.md` or incorporate its accepted facts and immutable reference identity in the PRD. Do not guess `--bind source` when no project source exists. After obtaining the Gate ID from `list`, invoke the same Gate runner with `attach --gate-id --status passed --evidence-type source_artifact --evidence-path docs/backend-requirements-prd.md --bind requirements`, or execute an applicable validator once with `run --gate-id --bind requirements -- `. Missing or empty PRD makes the binding unavailable. The requirements-only terminal “all in-scope requirements” Gate uses this closure and does not demand an implementation-coverage receipt; a change to any included evidence makes it stale. Every validation argv must itself fail closed: use no pipeline, or place `set -o pipefail`/`set -euo pipefail` inside the executed shell script before any pipeline; `tee` never turns an internal failure into a passing Gate. One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document and owns only `.domainry/development/.md`; never overwrite or update another session's document. A new session creates a new file even for related work and may reference prior session TODOs only as read-only handoff context. The TODO is the only progress ledger. Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to this document, finish the reachable round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate binds the artifact and exact fact proved. Changed evidence content or a bound source, requirements artifact, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, identity, or receipt-named artifact makes the Gate stale and requires current evidence. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs. The lightweight TODO checker only detects document consistency; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system. Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first. ## Round discipline For every validation round: 1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage. 2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence. 3. Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repeat until no open finding remains. Stop early only when continuation is impossible, risks data loss or security, corrupts protected state, or invalidates the remaining results. A recoverable failure is not a reason to stop the round. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation. For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey blocked by that root cause, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner once, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator. ## Project and frontend boundaries The canonical project-owned authoring surfaces are: ```text backend/model/*.json declarative backend metadata inventory backend/reports/*.sql project-owned Report SQL referenced by model sql_file backend/ project-owned Go source and tests plus generated platform source .domainry/development/.md current session TODO .domainry/ CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence ``` Git owns project-source development, so normal editors, patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source. `.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination exception under `.domainry/**`, with each file owned only by its matching Host session. Never hand-edit generated source; frozen Project Contracts; Runtime manifests; materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts; audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state. Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set. Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header: - `integration_authorized`: the user requested a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the task to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms project ownership; - `backend_only`: the user explicitly limited work to backend; - `externally_owned`: another tool or owner delivered the frontend; - `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation. The scope records authorization context only and never changes this Skill's edit boundary: `frontend/**` remains read-only in every scope throughout the task. During integration compare the requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response before assigning ownership. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a compatibility adapter, raw HTTP, fabricated fallback, altered Mock, or weakened test. Record a frontend- or Mock-owned defect as a finding with owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, and contract basis. If it blocks a backend journey, mark that journey blocked without relabeling the defect as a platform gap. End-to-end acceptance here means backend end-to-end through real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior bound to the TODO and Gate source identity. Browser-layer UI verification is outside this Skill's acceptance scope. ## New and existing projects For a new project: - Before any project-mutating `domainry-cli` command, require the exact project root to be one initialized Git worktree. If the new root is not inside another worktree, run `git init --initial-branch=main ` once and verify `git -C rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals the exact root. Changed bound content makes evidence stale, but a terminal Gate remains immutable; create a new repair-round Gate instead of rerunning it. `status`, `list`, receipt reads, and `attach` never execute the product command. Run module-focused Go tests against the completed current module batch before source finalization, then require `project check --scope actions` to pass before finalization. The check's stale-scaffold scan rejects a delivery-bound implemented Handler whose canonical generated test still invokes nil Execution or asserts that Action's `*.not_implemented` result, and returns the complete bounded stable diagnostic inventory without running tests or emitting source. For a dependency-resolved materialized Go backend with Actions it also performs the offline, readonly production compile closure for `./actions/...`; it disables workspace use, toolchain auto-download, VCS, and module/network lookup. Expected source-policy and compile failures remain contract-shaped JSON; launch/infrastructure failures remain diagnosable only through the bounded failure receipt. Finalize repeats the source preflight, activates local composition, closes dependencies, and enforces applicable compilation before publishing a success receipt. Failure publishes no new successful finalization receipt and rolls back activated changes where required. Later cross-module/full verification tests still require a current complete finalization receipt. Repair every failed round as one batch, then create a new round-specific Gate; `skipped_dependency` is not a pass. ### Accept authorization and navigation against real data Run this required acceptance after backend implementation and real Runtime/database data acceptance, before the apply stage can close: 1. Read the complete Action inventory from the current published Runtime metadata and record the total. 2. Write Action authorization matrix rows with delta scope. For a full batch (a new project or an increment that changes authorization broadly), write one row per published Action and require the matrix row count to equal the published total. For an existing-project increment, write one row per Action added or changed in this batch and one summary row per unchanged Action group that references the prior accepted matrix evidence (previous session TODO path and date); the batch rows plus referenced rows must still cover the published total. Each authored row records Action identity, target/Object, execution kind, published permission or exact `allowed_roles`, required data scope, one allowed probe, one denied probe, current Runtime or persisted evidence, and result. An Action without a permission owner, allowed role, required scope, or denied proof is a blocking mismatch. 3. Inspect the actual Runtime database through the supported project database/inspection path after seed and business-data acceptance. Record the query or durable evidence identifiers for persisted menu definitions, role-menu assignments, roles, and other permission state used by the matrix. Do not infer persisted state from Blueprint or source alone. 4. For every application role affected by this batch, the Agent creates or reuses a real Runtime session through a project-provisioned non-human acceptance identity and calls `GET /identity/effective-menus?surface=business_workspace`. For an existing-project increment, roles with no menu, permission, or route change in this batch may reference the prior accepted effective-menu evidence instead of a fresh session. Compare returned menu identities and routes with the persisted menu definitions and role-menu assignments. Record missing, unexpected, disabled, or cross-role entries. Never ask the user to log in, switch roles, repeat login, or provide personal credentials. Use the formal project seed/admin path to provision acceptance identities when authorized; otherwise record the missing safe identity/session path as an environment or Foundation blocker. 5. Record totals and the complete Action authorization and role-effective-menu matrices in the current TODO. Finish the whole round, batch-repair every mismatch, repeat the database/API comparisons, and proceed only when mismatch totals are zero. Metadata checklist success or isolated allow tests cannot replace this acceptance. ### Review and converge Run a complete backend/integration round covering APIs, business journeys, the completed authorization/navigation matrices, allowed/denied authorization, data-scope isolation, sensitive fields, durable effects, validation, conflicts, idempotency, Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, audit, and outbox. Finish the round before repair, then batch-repair by owner group and re-run the invalidated backend checks until no open finding remains (Round discipline). ## verify After the backend converges, read [evidence-levels.md](evidence-levels.md) and [verification.md](verification.md) completely and re-read [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md). `project verify` and packaging prove `delivery_verified` structural/release closure, not `scenario_verified` real-data behavior. Keep verification and packaging as two independent development Gates and execute their exact `project verify --json` and `project package --json` commands separately; neither command receipt can close the other Gate. Run the complete verify check-and-evidence inventory specified in verification — backend source boundary and suites, checklist/live validation, verify + package, managed Runtime, acceptance denominator prepare/harness/check, authorization/data-scope/idempotency journeys, matrix consistency, long/dense cases, and cleanup. Frontend build and test gates remain entirely outside Builder. Guide-specific ordering rules: Resolve Runtime start/status only through `--profile runtime-process-continuation --runtime-address ` with a fresh current Host session ID. When its TODO, Gate state, and Runtime profile are all absent, the resolver atomically creates the canonical minimal two-Gate TODO and both managed state files; do not instantiate or read the whole-project TODO template first. The profile alone owns the fixed `runtime_start` → `runtime_status` kinds, labels, Gate IDs, exact argv, bindings, packaged CLI, current bundle, address, and identities, and stdout contains only the compact remaining recipes. Never call either product command through generic `run`, copy controls, infer a Gate from prose, or read verification authorities or runner source to assemble controls. Re-resolving after start returns only status; completion or terminal failure never reopens a Gate, while partial, unsafe, non-owned, or conflicting state fails closed without overwrite. - validate that the source-finalization receipt is still current; if source changes during repair, return to finalization before compiling or testing; - confirm the persisted Action/permission and role/effective-menu matrices still match the restarted Runtime and accepted database. After the matching managed Runtime is healthy, run `project acceptance prepare`, then execute the platform runner **first** with `project acceptance run --cases standard` and inspect its exact-set v2 result rows. Build business harness assertions on `assets/acceptance-harness-core.py` only for `state:"not_passed"` rows with `disposition:"needs_business_harness"`. Repair `blocked_dependency`, `blocked_platform`, `unsupported_runner`, `setup_failed`, `evidence_rejected`, or `runtime_failed` at the named owner before rerunning. Then run `project acceptance check`. Every assertion obtains its session through `harness.session_for_case(case)`, uses `ScenarioGraph` for isolated setup/dependencies, and applies `ReasonOracle` for the declared status/error/state/audit/positive-control reason; never select a user from a role name, create profile headers, or read an internal identity table. The denominator is CLI-owned and never hand-edited. After a model evolution, run `project acceptance stale-report` and re-record only reported `stale`/`missing` cases, never the full set. Prose, arbitrary hashed text, or a coverage percentage cannot replace the harness. Record the whole verify round before repair. If any finding exists, return it to its model or implementation owner, repair the batch, and run verify again (Round discipline). ## done Record exactly one terminal state from [verification.md](verification.md): `done`, `acceptance_failed`, or `verification_blocked`, applying its failure classification and terminal policy. `done` requires every in-scope TODO item closed with concise current evidence, an empty finding inventory, a passing final verify round, every in-scope requirement mapped to implemented source and current validation evidence, and no requirement or limitation hidden, downgraded, or deferred. Product prerequisites such as identities, data, permissions, Runtime health, or persistence are implementation/Foundation defects, not environmental blockers. Do not claim `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done` above the highest evidence level reached; no structural pass upgrades delivery evidence into real-data behavior. For any terminal state, require the applicable `verify` and `done` Gate status, close every finding according to the terminal policy, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` immediately before the final response. Repair inconsistency and rerun until it passes. This linter pass is not test, Runtime, delivery, or scenario evidence. Provide a concise completion summary with implemented scope, test results, Runtime results, and explicitly non-blocking limitations. ## System seed login Runtime owns every initial credential. Never write credential rows, embed a password in model/source/TODO/evidence, or replace formal provisioning and password-change flows. A missing system/project seed credential is initialized from Runtime's deployment-owned `AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD`; production startup rejects the built-in development value and the credential is always marked `must_change_password:true`. A user created through the formal Identity API receives a cryptographically random per-user password exactly once in a `Cache-Control: no-store` response and must change it. Startup fills only a missing credential; it never overwrites an existing password hash, clears a lock, or undoes a changed password. The canonical system identity is user ID `admin`, login `admin@example.com`, Admin Console `/admin`, Surface `admin_console`. In a managed development Runtime started by this workflow, a deployment without `AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` seeds every missing credential — `admin` and project-declared acceptance identities — with development default `Domainry@2026`, marked `must_change_password:true`; production rejects this value. Establish a managed-development acceptance session by logging in with that default, completing forced change through `POST /auth/change-password` with `Idempotency-Key`, and keeping the new credential only in authorized secret handoff. Never print credentials into evidence or guess passwords: five failed logins produce `auth.account_locked`, and expiry does not lift the lock; an admin session must call `POST /identity/users/{userID}/unlock`. Formal Identity API users instead use their one-time no-store password. Business Workspace and Consumer Portal actors come from project-declared non-human acceptance identities. Authentication mode, session refresh, and authorization are independent of Surface; protected operations still enforce functional permission, ownership, Action policy, assurance, and data scope.

# Project development guide Drive every development batch with one visible project document: ```text /.domainry/development/.md ``` The complete frontend under `frontend/**` provides concrete demand evidence through routes, screens, typed APIs, Mock adapters, tests, states, and copy. It may omit business rules or encode provisional assumptions, so inspect it read-only while extracting requirements and domain truth. The CLI-compiled capability disclosure and Runtime machine contracts remain authoritative for data, authorization, navigation, and operation semantics. Frontend source and dependencies stay externally owned and read-only throughout the task; the recorded scope and evidence-based defect routing below turn frontend-owned defects into findings, never edits. See [backend-runtime.md](backend-runtime.md) for the closed backend Runtime boundary. The fixed stage order is: requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done. Requirements and domain facts always precede Runtime capability selection; platform shape never supplies business truth. ## Batch scale First record `Execution scope: requirements_only` or `implementation`. Use `requirements_only` only when the user requests analysis, requirements, or domain design and explicitly excludes development. It keeps the header, requirements, domain-truth design, and done sections; omit model, apply, Runtime, and verify sections with that reason in the header. Its `done` proves only the accepted requirements/domain artifact and must report no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim. Any build, repair, integration, or end-to-end request is `implementation` and follows the normal full/light rules below. Classify every batch as `full` or `light` and record the classification with its justification in the TODO header. A light batch is an existing-project increment with no new Object, Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change; everything else is a full batch. In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging. The caller-explicit `source-finalization-continuation` and `post-apply-source-finalization-continuation` routes are selected and initialized from the loaded entrypoint before any whole-project resource is read. They never load this guide, the TODO template, or another whole-project reference; each compact Gate-owned envelope is its complete workflow. For every normal whole-project session, use the following initialization unchanged. At the start of an Agent session: 1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once. 2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`. 3. Resolve the session ID from the resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; the temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, borrow, or reuse another session's ID. 4. If `.domainry/development/.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session. 5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`. 6. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, scope, one `Frontend mutation scope`, and `requirements` as the initial current stage before implementation. 7. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan. 8. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; never check later work merely because it happened out of order. Close checkboxes through the evidence Gate's `run`, `attach`, or explicit `mark --status not_applicable` commands, not by writing success prose. Before leaving a stage, require `status --stage --require-complete`. Before any Host resume, first prove the original Agent turn has actually ended; an outer exec wrapper reporting `Unknown process id`, losing its timing output, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence. Never start a second Agent against the same session TODO/Gates while the first may still be alive. 9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes. For `requirements_only`, the formal Gate identity is the deterministic requirements-evidence closure exposed as `requirements`: the mandatory non-empty `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`; root `requirements.md` when it exists; and, when `frontend/src/**` contains a regular source file, the complete regular-file evidence under `frontend/**` after excluding dependency, build, coverage, cache, database, log, backup, and temporary artifacts. Paths and content hashes are sorted and framed, so creation order, timestamps, worktree location, backend files, unrelated root files, and derived frontend files do not affect the identity; symlinks fail closed. A frontend-led or immutable external-reference PRD is valid without root `requirements.md`: the PRD records its authority and immutable frontend snapshot/commit or external citation, and the local frontend closure is bound automatically when present. Do not silently place another mutable local authority elsewhere; make it the canonical root `requirements.md` or incorporate its accepted facts and immutable reference identity in the PRD. Do not guess `--bind source` when no project source exists. After obtaining the Gate ID from `list`, invoke the same Gate runner with `attach --gate-id --status passed --evidence-type source_artifact --evidence-path docs/backend-requirements-prd.md --bind requirements`, or execute an applicable validator once with `run --gate-id --bind requirements -- `. Missing or empty PRD makes the binding unavailable. The requirements-only terminal “all in-scope requirements” Gate uses this closure and does not demand an implementation-coverage receipt; a change to any included evidence makes it stale. Every validation argv must itself fail closed: use no pipeline, or place `set -o pipefail`/`set -euo pipefail` inside the executed shell script before any pipeline; `tee` never turns an internal failure into a passing Gate. One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document and owns only `.domainry/development/.md`; never overwrite or update another session's document. A new session creates a new file even for related work and may reference prior session TODOs only as read-only handoff context. The TODO is the only progress ledger. Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to this document, finish the reachable round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate binds the artifact and exact fact proved. Changed evidence content or a bound source, requirements artifact, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, identity, or receipt-named artifact makes the Gate stale and requires current evidence. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs. The lightweight TODO checker only detects document consistency; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system. Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first. ## Round discipline For every validation round: 1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage. 2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence. 3. Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repeat until no open finding remains. Stop early only when continuation is impossible, risks data loss or security, corrupts protected state, or invalidates the remaining results. A recoverable failure is not a reason to stop the round. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation. For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey blocked by that root cause, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner once, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator. ## Project and frontend boundaries The canonical project-owned authoring surfaces are: ```text backend/model/*.json declarative backend metadata inventory backend/reports/*.sql project-owned Report SQL referenced by model sql_file backend/ project-owned Go source and tests plus generated platform source .domainry/development/.md current session TODO .domainry/ CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence ``` Git owns project-source development, so normal editors, patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source. `.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination exception under `.domainry/**`, with each file owned only by its matching Host session. Never hand-edit generated source; frozen Project Contracts; Runtime manifests; materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts; audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state. Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set. Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header: - `integration_authorized`: the user requested a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the task to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms project ownership; - `backend_only`: the user explicitly limited work to backend; - `externally_owned`: another tool or owner delivered the frontend; - `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation. The scope records authorization context only and never changes this Skill's edit boundary: `frontend/**` remains read-only in every scope throughout the task. During integration compare the requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response before assigning ownership. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a compatibility adapter, raw HTTP, fabricated fallback, altered Mock, or weakened test. Record a frontend- or Mock-owned defect as a finding with owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, and contract basis. If it blocks a backend journey, mark that journey blocked without relabeling the defect as a platform gap. End-to-end acceptance here means backend end-to-end through real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior bound to the TODO and Gate source identity. Browser-layer UI verification is outside this Skill's acceptance scope. ## New and existing projects For a new project: - Before any project-mutating `domainry-cli` command, require the exact project root to be one initialized Git worktree. If the new root is not inside another worktree, run `git init --initial-branch=main ` once and verify `git -C rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals the exact root. Never retry mutations before this check, initialize an existing project without authorization, or create a nested repository inside another worktree. - Preserve the full requirement; do not silently reduce it to an MVP, demo, phase, or core subset. - Establish users, roles, goals, lifecycles, exceptional paths, and the complete operation inventory before modeling. - Apply industry business practices where they clarify the requested product without expanding its scope. - Before first backend publication, model local/test-only non-human acceptance identities, their formal login/session path, required Workforce profiles and assignments, departments/jobs/positions, business menu definitions, role-menu assignments, and the minimum real records for every acceptance journey. The implementer may add the minimum contrasting identities needed to prove same-record allow/deny, data-Scope, and requester isolation; these are acceptance fixtures, not evidence of the product's organization size or role cardinality. Do not defer these prerequisites to verify or seed online credentials. For an existing project: - Read current requirement documents, Git state, backend source, metadata, tests, and managed delivery state. - Record current behavior and the affected dependency closure in the TODO. - Plan only the requested increment and required regression coverage. - Retain valid existing source; do not rewrite it to manufacture workflow evidence. ## Initialization Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once at task start. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, session ID, TODO, compact `resume_packet`, one-time `authoring_context`, routed reference paths, and package identity to the result. `DOMAINRY_CLI` must equal the same package's single executable `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. Never resolve a CLI through `PATH`, substitute another Skill, or call Domainry Plane directly. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. These actions are setup rather than stages or TODO gates. Use only the applicable command families below, in TODO order. Add one pinned `--environment ` or `--service ` target wherever shown and keep it consistent. Use `--help` only to resolve listed-command flags; do not invent neighboring commands. Do not move, copy, merge, or recreate the managed root by hand. ## requirements ### Produce the backend dependency PRD For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. This is not a marketing PRD or a pixel inventory: it is the accepted demand contract for what Runtime and project metadata/source must provide. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline. **Reference mode for structured input.** A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as ` §N`. Test per requirement: if one section states the rule completely, cite it — do not restate it; rewrite only what must be assembled from scattered evidence (Mock adapters, tests, verbal decisions, multiple documents). A reference-mode PRD carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section; restating an already-structured source is prohibited waste. Both modes keep the Resolve-critical-ambiguity table and full traceability. Read frontend evidence in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/fixtures; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Legacy APIs or prior backends are `legacy_reference` until the current requirement or frontend confirms them. This inspection is read-only even when later integration is authorized to repair frontend source. A Mock fixture, adapter behavior, test expectation, or visible affordance proves demand or a current assumption; it does not establish a business rule without higher-precedence evidence. Use this precedence when evidence conflicts: 1. explicit current user decision; 2. latest accepted requirement or design contract; 3. latest implemented frontend behavior; 4. typed API and Mock semantics; 5. frontend tests; 6. legacy/reference implementation. Do not erase conflicts using precedence alone. Record the conflict, affected requirement IDs, selected authority, and confirmation evidence. # Verification and terminal policy

Read this file completely on entry to `verify`, `done`, or terminal review after a repair.

## Verification closure

After `project verify`, package, and startup of the exact current managed Runtime, run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This creates the CLI-owned `.domainry/builder/acceptance/denominator.json`. Do not edit it. The denominator is generated from requirement IDs, every linked model resource, acceptance scenarios, typed Runtime operations, roles and exact data-scope declarations, plus capability-specific lifecycles. It also contains the mandatory `domainry-semantic-acceptance-contract-v1`: exactly one mapping per denominator case from requirement → actor → formal principal context → fresh setup → command operation → evidence facts → reason-specific oracle. Preparation and every later load fail closed if a mapping is missing or if its actor, command, fact closure, setup isolation, expected outcome/error, or HTTP oracle diverges from the denominator. Its hash binds the current model, Blueprint, capability lock, Runtime Domain API, delivery, Runtime manifest, verification/package receipts, Runtime binary, and stable database cohort identity. The live process PID is intentionally not part of that stable hash because a restart case must replace it; the typed restart artifact must bind the old PID, current new PID, unchanged database cohort, delivery, and binary. A model, capability, source, package, database target, or Runtime change requires a new denominator; `prepare` archives every generation under `.domainry/builder/acceptance/history/denominator/`, and previously recorded results survive an evolution only through the incremental staleness flow below — never by assumption.

The denominator must cover every changed or newly published operation plus referenced prior evidence for unchanged operations. Each case names its Runtime owner, actor/role, permission and data scope, required outcome, error contract, restart sensitivity, and required evidence kinds. Every scoped read and write requires positive and differentiated-scope proof (database-agnostic, by ordinary query/HTTP probes — never engine-level RLS posture; see G14); every protected operation also requires permission-denied proof. Writes additionally require missing-idempotency-key rejection, idempotent replay, idempotency conflict, persistence read-back and audit correlation. Project Actions additionally require one HTTP mutation per business intent, one Runtime unit of work, atomic commit, injected rollback, and concurrency conflict; atomicity is proven by `http_exchange` + `transaction_trace` + `persistence_snapshot` + `audit_correlation`. The denominator never reads frontend source or requires frontend evidence. Each declared Handler Connector call gets its own case bound to the exact connector, connection, provider, operation, execution mode and side-effect class; durable writes require worker restart and terminal reconciliation. Declared notification events require after-commit once-only durable refetch, and every external channel gets its own provider-terminal case. Every Report and typed list/search/query operation requires bounded page and stable traversal cases with a query profile captured on the same database cohort named by the managed process receipt: SQLite uses `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, MySQL uses `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, and PostgreSQL uses `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, all with statement/row-count observation and machine-checked index/full-scan classification. Evidence whose dialect or plan format differs from `runtime_identity.database_driver` is rejected; no second database or SQLite fallback is allowed. Its signed cursor must either encode the complete deterministic keyset tuple or bind an authorized source version to a bounded offset; a source-version-fenced continuation must reject source drift as a stale-cursor conflict. Automation Rules derive before-transaction rollback or after-commit restart/terminal cases from their trigger. Agent resources additionally require task cancel/retry/reconcile with terminal worker/audit evidence and interactive SSE disconnect/resume. A manual approval Workflow is proven as a durable process: start before the managed Runtime replacement, refetch after restart, decide real assigned tasks through participant APIs, and observe terminal persistence/audit; it does not claim `worker_terminal` unless the graph actually schedules worker-owned work. Scheduled jobs and governed report exports retain worker restart/resume evidence. Typed operations declared by acceptance `config.runtime_operations` must resolve to the pinned Runtime API and include both positive and denied rows for writes. Read and apply all 32 families in [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md); a project may mark a family not applicable only from model-derived evidence.

Semantic oracles are strict. Each scenario uses fresh setup identities/records or names an explicit dependency whose passing evidence is current. A positive case must identify and observe its intended target with the required non-empty facts; a `2xx` paired with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or different record is not proof unless that exact value is the confirmed outcome. A negative case must reach the intended stable status/error/concealment and prove unchanged durable state; an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, empty result caused by bad setup, or exception from a missing dependency is not the expected rejection. Scope isolation probes use otherwise equivalent requests against the same target through formal matching and non-matching Runtime sessions, plus the broader in-scope role when applicable. Runtime-owned identity/context values in setup and requests must come from the formal typed client, seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime result and be carried unchanged; synthetic claims or hand-normalized canonical values invalidate the case.

### Runner-first acceptance execution

With the denominator prepared and the managed Runtime healthy, execute the mechanical case families through the platform runner FIRST — before writing any harness code:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The runner (capability `project.acceptance.run`, diagnostic report contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-run-v2`) mechanically executes the standard Action, Automation, Report GET-summary, Runtime read-route, Workflow, governed export and Scheduler families against the live Runtime and the exact sqlite/mysql/postgres database cohort bound by its managed process receipt, validates every artifact with the same `acceptance check` validators before writing it, and atomically writes/merges one complete `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2` document. External cohorts require the same explicit `DATABASE_DRIVER`/`DATABASE_DSN` environment binding already used by the managed Runtime; the runner compares only non-secret DSN/cohort identities and never serializes the DSN. It contains exactly one row per denominator case: `passed`, `declared_gap`, or `not_passed` with typed responsibility. Existing passed/gap rows are immutable; existing `not_passed` rows are retried. The separate `.domainry/development/acceptance-evidence/backend-acceptance-run.json` is execution diagnostics, not a second source of case truth. For every case the runner uses the semantic contract's exact actor and calls the authenticated Runtime `GET /identity/principal-context` resolver; Runtime returns canonical workspace/workforce/organization/business-profile/surface selectors, and the runner carries only those selectors into requests. Neither runner nor business harness may infer a user from role ordering, construct profile headers, or query Runtime-owned identity tables. Never re-implement or overwrite a runner-passed case. A `not_passed` outcome with `disposition:"runtime_failed"` is an observed contract violation — a product defect to repair at its owner, never a harness problem. Only `needs_business_harness` rows belong in the self-built harness. `blocked_dependency`, `blocked_platform`, `unsupported_runner`, `setup_failed`, `evidence_rejected`, and `runtime_failed` return to their named owner first; downstream cases sharing a failed setup are `blocked_dependency`, not independent failures.

Self-built harness code must be a thin assertion layer on top of [acceptance-harness-core.py](../assets/acceptance-harness-core.py): copy that file unchanged into `.domainry/development/`, then write only per-case assertion functions against it — never re-implement session/auth bootstrap, HTTP or database capture, artifact/evidence/results writers, resume state, or retry/backoff plumbing. SQLite is stdlib-backed. A MySQL/PostgreSQL cohort passes one DB-API 2 `database_connector(driver, dsn, schema)` callback to `Harness`; core code suppresses connector stdout/stderr, verifies the in-database cohort marker, owns dialect SQL/EXPLAIN and DSN/password redaction, and fails explicitly if the adapter is absent or mismatched—there is no SQLite fallback. Use `harness.session_for_case(case)` exclusively for the frozen actor/principal mapping. Register cases in `ScenarioGraph`; each setup receives a fresh opaque namespace, `setup_failed` is distinct from a product failure, and downstream cases become `blocked_dependency` rather than executing against missing residue. Apply `ReasonOracle` for exact positive, rejection, state, scope, and audit assertions before sealing evidence.

Execute only the remaining `needs_business_harness` cases through that real acceptance harness and project-provisioned non-human Runtime identities. The harness—not prose editing—writes typed HTTP exchanges, SSE transcripts, durable refetches, idempotency receipts, database snapshots, transaction and pagination traces, query profiles, audit correlation, differentiated-scope data, provider receipts, worker terminal observations, and restart observations under project-owned `backend/tests/evidence/**`. Self-built harness code and every intermediate working file live under `.domainry/development/**` from the very first file, never anywhere under `backend/**`: harness files inside `backend/**` dirty the finalized `source_sha256` and make every gate receipt stale, and the measured cost of that mistake is a full finalize/verify/package redo plus re-recording all evidence. Every structured observation references one real regular non-symlink artifact and its SHA-256; persistence evidence also supplies before/after hashes and, for replay, the replay hash. Results and every evidence document bind the denominator and Runtime identity hashes. Then run:

The result document contract is `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2`: copy `denominator_sha256`, `runtime_identity`, and `runtime_identity_sha256` exactly from the denominator and provide exactly one `results[]` row for every denominator case. A `passed` row contains `case_id`, `state`, and `evidence[]` (`path`, `sha256`); a `not_passed` row contains no evidence and requires `outcome.disposition`, stable `code`, `owner`, `root_case_id`, `retryable`, and factual `reason`; a `declared_gap` row uses the existing typed gap contract. `acceptance check` fails closed while any `not_passed` row remains. The business harness may replace only a row whose disposition is `needs_business_harness`; it cannot replace platform, dependency, setup, evidence, unsupported-runner, or Runtime failures. Each referenced evidence document is `domainry-backend-acceptance-evidence-v1` with `state:"passed"`, the exact case/denominator/Runtime hashes, and `observations[]`. An observation has `kind`, project-relative `artifact`, `artifact_sha256`, and only for `persistence_snapshot` the required `before_sha256`/`after_sha256` plus replay SHA when applicable. Each artifact is strict JSON `domainry-backend-acceptance-artifact-v1` and binds its kind, case, operation, Runtime identity, producer source receipt, capture owner, and typed facts. Accepted kinds are `http_exchange`, `persistence_snapshot`, `idempotency_receipt`, `sse_transcript`, `durable_refetch`, `runtime_restart`, `worker_terminal`, `differentiated_scope_data`, `transaction_trace`, `pagination_trace`, `query_profile`, `audit_correlation`, `security_posture`, and `provider_receipt`. Pagination facts bind stable sort/tie-breaker and cursor strategy; offset fencing additionally requires the bound source version and observed stale-cursor rejection. Provider receipts bind the denominator's exact connector, connection, provider, operation; a durable provider or notification audit also requires its outbox reference. A correctly hashed arbitrary text file or a typed artifact whose endpoint, actor, outcome, transaction counts, page facts, process/database identity, differentiated data scope, or provider terminal state contradicts the denominator is rejected. The harness must preserve secrets safely, but redaction cannot remove facts needed to prove the case.

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The check reruns model derivation, resolves the live managed Runtime cohort, verifies every raw artifact, and requires exact set equality with the denominator. Missing, orphan, duplicate, failed, stale, unbound, unknown-kind, artifactless, or `self_reported` coverage fails. A percentage, prose claim, Mock transcript, or evidence from another Runtime can never satisfy it.

### Incremental re-recording after a model evolution

The denominator's `artifact_manifest` digests each operation's dependency closure, so an evolution no longer forces a blind full re-record: evidence recorded against an archived earlier generation stays binding when a complete hash proof chain shows nothing its case depends on changed. After any evolution, with the new denominator prepared, first run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The report (contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-stale-report-v1`) classifies every case as `current` (evidence still binds), `stale` (with reason), `missing`, or `declared_gap`, plus counts. Re-record ONLY the `stale` + `missing` subset. For the runner's mechanical families, re-run `project acceptance run --cases standard` on the same results file: it applies the same per-case carry-forward proof, keeps every `current` result (report field `carried_forward`), rebinds the file to the new denominator, and re-executes only what it dropped. For the remaining stale business-assertion cases, re-record through the harness core's stale-list resume — `stale_case_ids(<stale-report>)` plus `Harness(..., stale_report=...)` and `pending_cases(...)` — which rewrites only the affected result entries (evidence file paths are reused) instead of rebuilding the results file. Then run `acceptance check` as usual: a receipt with non-zero `carried_forward_cases` is a normal, complete result — carried-forward coverage is hash-proven, never a gap and never `self_reported`.

Carry-forward pays only when the repair converges on attributable model items (actions, workflows, reports, export controls, scheduled jobs, agent tasks — plus a report's own `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`). Any other project source change — handler code, config, anything else under `backend/**` — and any shared-collection change (objects, roles, workspaces, automation rules, seeds, ...) shifts the shared digest and makes every case stale; prefer model-item-level fixes and keep every working file out of `backend/**` (harness location discipline above).

Finish the complete verification round before repair. Preserve every first failure and continue safe checks to collect the full finding inventory. Then return findings to `requirements`, `model`, or `apply`, repair them together, and create new round-specific Gates for every invalidated command; a terminal Gate and its first receipt are never overwritten or rerun.

The CLI makes this concrete for local structural checks. A failed metadata checklist writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/checklist-failed.json`; a failed source finalization writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/finalization-failed.json`; a failed `project verify` writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/verification-failed.json`. Each check is `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped_dependency`. Safe independent checks run in the same round even when a sibling fails; dependency-bound checks are skipped explicitly.
