# Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract; frontend dependency installation and package wiring are outside this Skill.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, BFF, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. Application-facing client selection and wiring belong to the frontend owner outside this Skill; Builder models only the Application Delivery-published `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, stop and record the exact platform owner gap instead of adding an HTTP endpoint.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}/run`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/records/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Backend acceptance wraps typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, Product Surface, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request (gate: G04). For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

Start and inspect only through the machine-owned `runtime-process-continuation` profile returned by `domainry-development-context.py`, using a fresh current Host session ID and an explicit numeric loopback address such as `127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. Do not create a TODO first: the resolver atomically owns its canonical minimal TODO, state, profile, current project-relative bundle, packaged CLI, Gate IDs, exact argv, and source/Runtime/cohort bindings. Execute only its returned `run_recipes` in order. Stop with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project <project>` after acceptance. The managed receipt records the address, so subsequent acceptance commands use the same Runtime cohort. Do not load whole-project instructions for this compact recovery, background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or assemble Runtime Gate controls by hand.

The profile records start and current health as its two fixed machine Gates, `runtime_start` then `runtime_status`; they do not belong in the whole-project TODO template. The profile alone executes them. Both Gates require the `domainry-managed-runtime-process-v3` response/receipt and bind the current source, Runtime manifest, and exact managed process/database cohort. Neither Gate closes the broader acceptance-session and differentiated-data readiness item.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. Use task-published database evidence paths; do not rediscover private schema.

Stop Runtime and reclaim ports and processes after scenarios. A running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These idioms come from real Handler defects observed at runtime; `project source finalize`, compile, tests, and `project check` do NOT catch any of them.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Unlike the idioms below, `project source finalize` DOES reject the following three contracts (`backend_technical_contract` check), so each violation costs a failed-finalize round-trip — one real run hit 8 violations at once. Check every Handler before finalizing: (1) no generated capability I/O inside any loop (`for`/`range`) or recursive call cycle — do pure selection into bounded slices and call the generated batch/query capability once outside the loop; (2) every List query declares `Page(page, pageSize)` with a literal page size from 1 through 200 — an unpaged first result is forbidden; (3) no discarded call result or error — assign every capability return and handle every error. Generated batch inputs are 1 through 200, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal accepted fan-out shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's own `project verify` supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
```


# In-app notifications

> **TL;DR** — Owns: personal Inbox, unread badge, actionable station messages, notification preferences. Read when: requirements include a notification center or user-impacting event messages. Never: surface operational errors as user notifications.

## Problem and owner

Runtime Notification owns the personal Inbox for Business Workspace and Consumer Portal: durable user-impacting events, recipient resolution, localized immutable message snapshots, unread/read/archive state, alert acknowledgement, semantic actions, preferences, deduplication, aggregation, and optional external delivery. It is a user-facing projection, not an audit log, generic error sink, or Admin notification-template page.

## Supported model and Blueprint expression

Reason in this order:

```text
source-owned event → trusted rule and recipient resolution → Inbox item → optional email/collaboration/WhatsApp delivery
```

Use an Inbox message only when the event has a real user impact, resolvable recipient users, a stable event type and source-event/deduplication identity, actionable or durable informational value, and redacted variables. Keep request validation errors on the current page; keep internal logs, ordinary 4xx responses, unowned Runtime failures, and operator-only incidents in their owning error or observability surface.

Runtime currently publishes built-in Inbox event families for Workflow tasks, Scheduler failures/recovery, Integration credential/quota/billing health, record batch jobs, Report snapshots, and Automation execution results. These producers emit typed `NotificationIntent` facts; they do not supply rendered copy, arbitrary URLs, or HTTP requests. Prefer the built-in event generated by the owning capability instead of creating a project notification Action around the same lifecycle.

Domain Blueprint supports `notification_event_types[]` and `notification_rules[]` for project-owned Inbox events. A project Action may opt into the stable `notification.intent.dispatch` operation by listing exact published keys in `handler.notification_event_types[]`. The generated Action context then exposes only `capabilities.Notifications.Dispatch` and its bounded `DispatchBatch`; Runtime validates the grant and recipient, compiles immutable copy/actions from the published event type, and stages the event in the same database transaction as the Action's record mutation. `DispatchBatch` accepts 1 through 200 intents, returns receipt IDs one-to-one in input order, preflights the full input, and adds no notification to the Action session if any validation, grant, duplicate source identity, or compilation step fails. Every item inherits the invocation Workspace, Principal, grants, and Scope. Within a batch each `(event_type, source_event_id)` must be unique; persisted source identity and each required `dedupe_key` keep downstream replay/delivery deduplicated. Therefore:

- a Blueprint notification template does not create an Inbox event, choose recipients, or trigger delivery;
- Workflow `cc`, Automation `emit_event`, and `execution.result_notification` must not be assumed to create an arbitrary Inbox message; only a wired Runtime source owner publishing a typed Notification Intent crosses this boundary;
- a project event type used by an Action must publish a `project_record` semantic route action; literal URLs, private HTTP, direct database access, rendered copy from a Handler, and project-owned Inbox tables remain forbidden;
- `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` must carry exact recipient user IDs, stable `source_event_id`, business object key, record ID, exact business/order version, deduplication identity, Surface, occurrence time, and typed variables. The Action must also make a real business record mutation; notification-only Actions fail closed before commit.

## Authoring schema for `notification_event_types[]`

A project event type emitted from a `resource` model item uses exactly this shape. Required fields: `key`, `source`, `category`, `default_severity`, `surfaces`, `mandatory_in_app`, `template_key`, `default_locale`, `locales`, `version` (integer), `status` (must be `"published"`). Optional: `variables`, `actions`, `audience_resolvers` — but every `{{placeholder}}` used in any locale's copy **must** be declared in `variables[]` (`backend.notification.event_type_variable_unknown` otherwise). Each variables entry is `{"key","type","required"?}` with `type` from the closed enum `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `email`, `number`, `text`, `url` (there is no `string`). `locales` is an **object** mapping each locale (`zh_CN`-style, matching `^[A-Za-z]{2,3}(_[A-Za-z]{2})?$`) to the immutable in-app copy `{"title","body"}` (optional `facts`); there is no separate `content` property. Each `actions[]` entry is `{"key","kind":"route","resource_type","surface_routes":{<surface>:<route_key>}}` — `kind` only accepts `route`, and there are no `name`/`description`/`severity`/`surface`/`object_key` properties anywhere in the entry. When `actions[]` is declared, **every locale must also carry `action_labels`** mapping each action key to its localized label (e.g. `"action_labels": {"open_ticket": "查看工单"}`); a missing label fails compile with `backend.notification.event_type_action_label_missing`.

Validated example (in-app assignment notification dispatched by a Handler):

```json
{"collection": "notification_event_types", "key": "ticket.assigned", "value": {
  "key": "ticket.assigned", "source": "project", "category": "business",
  "default_severity": "info", "surfaces": ["business_workspace"],
  "mandatory_in_app": true, "template_key": "ticket_assigned",
  "default_locale": "zh_CN",
  "locales": {
    "zh_CN": {"title": "工单已分派给你", "body": "工单「{{ticket_title}}」已分派给你处理。",
              "action_labels": {"open_ticket": "查看工单"}},
    "en_US": {"title": "Ticket assigned to you", "body": "Ticket \"{{ticket_title}}\" was assigned to you.",
              "action_labels": {"open_ticket": "View ticket"}}
  },
  "variables": [{"key": "ticket_title", "type": "text", "required": true}],
  "actions": [{"key": "open_ticket", "kind": "route", "resource_type": "project_record",
               "surface_routes": {"business_workspace": "business.tickets.my"}}],
  "version": 1, "status": "published"
}}
```

`notification_templates[]` entries are for **external delivery channels only** — the `channel` enum is `email`, `collaboration`, `whatsapp`; there is no `in_app` channel. In-app copy lives in the event type's `locales`, so a purely in-app notification declares no template entry at all. Do not add a template just to satisfy `template_key`; that key is the stable identity of the compiled in-app copy.

Example declaration and call:

```json
{"handler":{"notification_event_types":["business_task.assigned"]}}
```

```go
_, err := capabilities.Notifications.Dispatch(ctx, capabilities.AssignNotificationIntent{
    EventType: "business_task.assigned", SourceEventID: eventID,
    RecipientUserIDs: []string{recipientID}, Surface: "business_workspace",
    SubjectObjectKey: "business_task", SubjectRecordID: taskID,
    SubjectVersion: orderVersion, DedupeKey: eventID, OccurredAt: occurredAt,
})
```

For fan-out, build `[]capabilities.AssignNotificationIntent` in a pure loop and call `capabilities.Notifications.DispatchBatch(ctx, intents)` once outside the loop. Return any error so the Runtime-owned Action transaction rolls back all business mutations and staged Inbox events together.

For an existing built-in event, record the Inbox demand and its published Runtime operations when the product requires it; do not model notifications as project records. Frontend package selection and wiring remain owned by the frontend project and outside this Skill.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions

Keep Product Surfaces separate. Personal Inbox routes exist under Business Workspace and Consumer Portal; Admin Console owns notification governance and has no personal inbox. Do not reuse `/admin/system/notifications` as the user Inbox.

Persisted actions are semantic references. Resolve an action through Runtime for the current user and Surface, then navigate using the returned route key and parameters. Never persist or execute an arbitrary URL/API request from message content. Team Inbox access is read-only; it does not grant authority to mutate another user's mailbox or the referenced business resource.

An external delivery failure must not roll back an already materialized Inbox item. Conversely, a successful email or collaboration receipt is not proof that the user's Inbox item, unread count, or action exists.

## Examples

Correct: a Workflow assignment publishes `workflow.task.assigned`; the assignee sees one Business Workspace Inbox item and an unread-count increment, resolves `workflow.task.open` through Runtime, and then acts on the separately authorized Workflow task.

Correct: a Scheduler repeated failure produces a deduplicated warning/alert for the resolved operator; recovery updates the alert lifecycle. The page does not turn every scheduler log line into a user notification.

Wrong: declare an email `notification_templates[]` entry and claim the user now has an Inbox message. Wrong: create a project `notification` Object and custom CRUD UI to simulate Runtime Inbox. Wrong: show a success toast after a source event without independently reading the durable Inbox item.

Acceptance must prove the intended producer event, correct recipient and Product Surface, no leakage to a different user, durable item, unread/facet reconciliation, read/unread and archive/restore behavior when exposed, deduplication on replay, and safe action resolution. Test stream synchronization separately from persistence; an SSE `notification.sync` event is a refresh signal, not the notification record itself.

Lifecycle evidence uses the existing Inbox contract: event `materialized` plus item `created_at` is delivered; the first `read_at` transition is the durable first-open/read marker; an alert `acknowledged_at` or terminal `action_state` is handled. Do not invent a parallel delivery-status table merely to rename these states.

## Authority and limits

Owners: `pkg/runtimeext/notification.go`, `internal/runtime/application/action/action_executor_mutation.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/notification/model/notification_event_type_models.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/notification/model/notification_inbox_models.go`, `internal/runtime/application/notification/notification_inbox_application_service.go`, `internal/runtime/transport/http/notifications/notifications_routes.go`, `internal/runtime/bootstrap/runtime/startup.go`, `frontend/packages/runtime-client/src/index.ts`, `internal/controlplane/blueprint/model/contract.go`, `internal/controlplane/blueprint/compiler/runtime_manifest.go`, and `internal/controlplane/domaincodegen/action_context.go`. The exact methods in the active Application Delivery package declarations remain authoritative.
